scenario: A 53-year-old man's routine basic metabolic panel contains one physiologically impossible result (serum potassium of 54 mmol/L, a likely decimal/unit error) among otherwise normal values.
instruction: Review the laboratory observations in this bundle. Flag any value that is physiologically impossible or otherwise implausible for the analyte reported. For each flag, state its severity, describe the implausible value and why it cannot be a true measurement, and cite the source Observation as evidence. Do not flag values that are clinically plausible, even if you would normally expect a different number. If there are no implausible values, return an empty flag list.
